[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "title": "One-Dimensional Kinematic Foundations: Position, Displacement, and Trajectory Functions",
    "scope": "Establishes the fundamental reference frame and coordinate representations for one-dimensional rectilinear kinematics. Distinguishes between spatial position along an oriented axis, scalar distance covered along a path, and vector displacement across time intervals. Details standard physical units, dimensional notation, and functional position equations for particles moving along a straight line.",
    "key_points": [
      "Origin selection, reference frames, and coordinate axes with directional polarity (positive to the right, negative to the left)",
      "Displacement definition as a vector quantity along a single axis: $\\Delta x = x_2 - x_1$, possessing both magnitude and algebraic sign",
      "Path distance $S$ versus coordinate displacement $\\Delta x$, highlighting that distance is cumulative and intrinsically non-negative",
      "Standard units and conversion factors: $\\text{m}$, $\\text{km}$, $\\text{cm}$, $\\text{s}$, $\\text{h}$, $\\text{m/s}$, $\\text{m/s}^2$, $\\text{m/s}^3$, $\\text{km/h}$, $\\text{cm/s}$",
      "Functional representations of 1D position over time $x(t)$, including stationary baselines, linear shifts, and polynomial models such as $x(t) = 12t^2 - 2t^3$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "title": "Rates of Rectilinear Motion: Average Velocity versus Average Speed",
    "scope": "Contrasts directional displacement rates with scalar path rates over finite time intervals. Teaches the geometric interpretation of average velocity as a secant slope on position-time graphs and resolves classical travel paradoxes arising from naive arithmetic averages. Provides rigorous calculation methods for composite multi-stage journeys.",
    "key_points": [
      "Average velocity formula: $v_{\\text{avg}} = \\bar{v} = \\frac{\\Delta x}{\\Delta t} = \\frac{x_2 - x_1}{t_2 - t_1}$, defined by displacement and carrying an algebraic sign",
      "Average speed formula: $s_{\\text{avg}} = \\frac{\\text{total distance}}{\\Delta t}$, defined by total scalar path traveled",
      "Geometric realization of $v_{\\text{avg}}$ as the slope of the secant line intersecting $(t_1, x_1)$ and $(t_2, x_2)$ on an $x(t)$ plot",
      "The uphill-downhill round-trip problem ($30\\text{ km/h}$ up, $60\\text{ km/h}$ back): derivation of the harmonic mean $s_{\\text{avg}} = \\frac{2d}{d/30 + d/60} = 40\\text{ km/h}$, demonstrating invariance to distance and invalidity of arithmetic averaging",
      "Multi-stage trip analysis (the stranded truck): computing overall displacement, cumulative elapsed time, secant velocity ($16.8\\text{ km/h}$), and total journey average speed ($9.05\\text{ km/h}$)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "title": "Instantaneous Kinematics: Derivatives, Velocity, Speed, and Acceleration",
    "scope": "Develops the infinitesimal calculus formulation of rectilinear motion from the limit of finite intervals. Defines instantaneous velocity, scalar speed, and instantaneous acceleration as successive time derivatives of position. Introduces acceleration scales, earth gravity multiples, and the physical sign conventions governing speeding up versus slowing down.",
    "key_points": [
      "Instantaneous velocity definition: $v = \\lim_{\\Delta t \\to 0} \\frac{\\Delta x}{\\Delta t} = \\frac{dx}{dt}$, representing the tangent slope to $x(t)$",
      "Instantaneous speed as velocity magnitude $|v|$: operation of vehicular speedometers and sign-blindness",
      "Evaluation of functional forms: recognizing constant velocity ($x(t) = 3t - 2$, $x(t) = -2$), accelerating motion, and directional polarity ($v < 0$ for $x(t) = -4t^2 - 2$ and $x(t) = 2/t^2$)",
      "Instantaneous acceleration as the derivative of velocity and second derivative of position: $a = \\frac{dv}{dt} = \\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}$",
      "Units of acceleration and earth gravity baseline: $1g = 9.8\\text{ m/s}^2$ and passenger experience benchmarks (e.g., $3g \\approx 29.4\\text{ m/s}^2$ on roller coasters)",
      "Kinematic sign criteria: speed increases when $v$ and $a$ share identical signs (speeding up); speed decreases when $v$ and $a$ have opposing signs (braking/deceleration)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "title": "Graphical Kinematics and Feature Extraction from Curves",
    "scope": "Teaches systematic extraction of kinematic behavior across vertically aligned position, velocity, and acceleration curves. Covers physical interpretation of inflection points, tangent construction, and piecewise constant-acceleration segments. Formulates methods to identify where instantaneous velocity equals mean velocity directly from experimental curves.",
    "key_points": [
      "Three-tier aligned motion graphs ($x(t)$, $v(t)$, $a(t)$) exemplified by an ascending elevator cab: reading constant slopes as constant velocities, parabolic segments as uniform accelerations, and flat segments as zero rates",
      "Step discontinuities in $a(t)$ corresponding to kinks/slope changes in $v(t)$ ($+2\\text{ m/s}^2$ upward acceleration, $0\\text{ m/s}^2$ cruise at $4\\text{ m/s}$, $-4\\text{ m/s}^2$ deceleration)",
      "Extracting kinematic parameters from distance-time curves $S(t)$: inflection points representing peak velocity",
      "Tangent line method: locating time $t_0$ where instantaneous velocity $v(t_0)$ equals running mean velocity $\\bar{v}(t_0)$ via the ray drawn from the coordinate origin tangent to $S(t)$",
      "Polynomial extrema analysis on $x(t) = 12t^2 - 2t^3$: locating stationary points ($v = 0$), turnaround positions, peak velocity via $\\frac{dv}{dt} = 0$, and acceleration at rest instants"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "title": "Motion Under Constant Acceleration: Direct and Integral Formulations",
    "scope": "Derives the canonical kinematic equations of uniformly accelerated motion using both algebraic averaging and calculus integration. Details single and nested double integrals to reconstruct velocity and position from known initial conditions. Explores delayed-start pursuit scenarios characterized by constant-acceleration pursuit curves.",
    "key_points": [
      "Equivalence of average and instantaneous acceleration when $a(t) = \\text{const}$: $a = a_{\\text{avg}} = \\frac{v - v_0}{t}$",
      "First integration for velocity: $v(T) = v_i + \\int_0^T a(t)\\,dt \\implies v(t) = v_0 + at$",
      "Second integration for position: $x(T) = x_i + \\int_0^T v(t)\\,dt = x_i + v_i T + \\int_0^T dt \\int_0^t a(h)\\,dh \\implies x(t) = x_0 + v_0 t + \\frac{1}{2}at^2$",
      "Path length integral in unidirectional rectilinear motion: $S = \\int v(t)\\,dt$",
      "Pursuit with delayed onset: motorist moving at constant speed $v_c$ overtaken by a police motorcycle accelerating from rest at $a_m$ after reaction latency $\\Delta t_d$, setting $x_c(t) = x_m(t)$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "title": "Variable Acceleration Dynamics: Time- and Position-Dependent Integration",
    "scope": "Addresses non-constant acceleration problems where acceleration depends explicitly on time or spatial position. Introduces the chain-rule transformation connecting acceleration, velocity, and spatial displacement. Demonstrates analytic integration for exponential temporal decays and linear spatial gradients.",
    "key_points": [
      "Integration of time-dependent acceleration $a(t) = a_0 \\exp(-t/\\tau)$ with $v(0) = 0$: obtaining terminal velocity $v_{\\max} = a_0 \\tau$",
      "Closed-form position expression for exponential driving: $x(t) = \\int_0^t v(t')\\,dt' = a_0 \\tau \\left[ t - \\tau \\left(1 - e^{-t/\\tau}\\right) \\right]$",
      "The kinematic chain rule for position-dependent acceleration: $a = \\frac{dv}{dt} = \\frac{dv}{ds}\\frac{ds}{dt} = v\\frac{dv}{ds} = \\frac{1}{2}\\frac{d(v^2)}{ds}$",
      "Separation of variables for spatial acceleration profiles: $\\int_{v_0}^v v'\\,dv' = \\int_{s_0}^s a(s')\\,ds'$",
      "The tram stopping problem: solving $v\\frac{dv}{ds} = a_0 - bs$ between two stops ($v = 0$) to prove travel distance $AB = \\frac{2a_0}{b}$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "title": "Geometric Constraints and Coupled Motion Systems",
    "scope": "Develops the kinematic method of constraints for rigid and mechanically linked bodies. Teaches how to formulate coordinate invariants from geometry and differentiate with respect to time to extract velocity relationships. Analyzes sliding rods and moving wedge-guide mechanisms.",
    "key_points": [
      "Formulation of holonomic geometric constraints relating mechanical degrees of freedom",
      "Wedge-and-follower mechanism: vertical guide rod on a horizontal wedge of inclination $\\alpha$ moving with speed $u$, establishing $h = d\\tan\\alpha$ and $v = u\\tan\\alpha$",
      "Rigid rod sliding between perpendicular floor and wall: Pythagorean constraint $OA^2 + OB^2 = l^2$",
      "Time-dependent position of sliding rod end: $Y_B(t) = \\sqrt{l^2 - (x_0 + vt)^2}$ for uniform floor velocity $v$",
      "Differentiating geometric constraints to reveal non-uniform, diverging velocity and acceleration profiles at extreme angles"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "title": "Relative Motion, Collisions, and Pursuit Problems",
    "scope": "Treats two-body and multi-body interactions across inertial reference frames. Formulates the vector collinearity criterion required for mutual particle interception. Covers pursuit kinematics under head starts, bounded maximum-speed durations, symmetrical pursuit geometries, and accelerated frames.",
    "key_points": [
      "Vector condition for collision of two particles moving uniformly: $\\vec{r}_1 + \\vec{v}_1 t = \\vec{r}_2 + \\vec{v}_2 t \\implies \\frac{\\vec{r}_1 - \\vec{r}_2}{|\\vec{r}_1 - \\vec{r}_2|} = \\frac{\\vec{v}_2 - \\vec{v}_1}{|\\vec{v}_2 - \\vec{v}_1|}$",
      "Invariant travel time shortcut: resolving the trains-and-bird problem via total train collision duration $t = \\frac{D}{2V_{\\text{train}}}$ without summing infinite geometric series",
      "One-dimensional bounded pursuit: cheetah ($101\\text{ km/h}$) hunting antelope ($88\\text{ km/h}$), catch time under initial spatial gap, and maximum catchable head start within sprint endurance $t_{\\max} = 20\\text{ s}$",
      "Symmetrical multi-agent pursuit: three particles at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side $a$ continuously targeting each other with constant speed $v$",
      "Decomposition of mutual approach velocity along connecting lines: $-\\frac{dl}{dt} = v + v\\cos(\\pi/3) = \\frac{3}{2}v$, yielding convergence time $t = \\frac{2a}{3v}$",
      "Accelerating reference frames: bolt falling from ceiling in an elevator ascending with acceleration $a_e$, solving motion in cabin frame ($a_{\\text{rel}} = g + a_e$) versus shaft frame"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "title": "Supersonic Kinematics: Acoustic Waves and Mach Cones",
    "scope": "Examines wave propagation emitted by sources traveling faster than the phase velocity of the medium. Constructs the geometric envelope of spherical wavefronts forming the Mach cone in supersonic flight. Derives the mathematical link between vehicle altitude, acoustic arrival delay, and Mach velocity.",
    "key_points": [
      "Wavefront envelopes produced by subsonic versus supersonic source velocities",
      "Mach cone geometry: tangency of spherical acoustic wavefronts emitted at successive points along the path",
      "Mach angle relation: $\\sin\\alpha = \\frac{c t'}{u t'} = \\frac{c}{u} = \\frac{1}{M}$, where $c$ is the speed of sound and $u$ is vehicle speed",
      "Geometric relation for an observer at ground level: linking altitude $H$, delay time $t$ elapsed after overhead flyover, and horizontal ground offset",
      "Analytical derivation of flight speed: $u t = \\frac{H}{c}\\sqrt{u^2 - c^2}$, yielding the explicit formula $u = \\frac{H c}{\\sqrt{H^2 - c^2 t^2}}$"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 10,
    "title": "Curvilinear Trajectories: Intrinsic Coordinates, Curvature, and Acceleration Components",
    "scope": "Establishes natural intrinsic coordinate systems for arbitrary two-dimensional curved trajectories. Derives the rigorous decomposition of acceleration into orthogonal tangential and normal vectors using the radius of curvature. Applies this decomposition to complex spiral paths with variable acceleration profiles.",
    "key_points": [
      "Natural coordinate representation: arc length $l$, unit tangent vector $\\vec{\\tau}$, and unit principal normal vector $\\vec{n}$ pointing toward the center of curvature",
      "Velocity in intrinsic components: $\\vec{v} = v_\\tau \\vec{\\tau} = \\frac{dl}{dt}\\vec{\\tau}$",
      "Derivation of the rate of change of the tangent vector: $\\frac{d\\vec{\\tau}}{dt} = v_\\tau \\frac{d\\vec{\\tau}}{dl} = \\frac{v_\\tau}{\\rho}\\vec{n}$, via the infinitesimal geometry $|d\\vec{\\tau}| = \\delta\\alpha = \\frac{dl}{\\rho}$",
      "Full acceleration decomposition: $\\vec{a} = a_\\tau \\vec{\\tau} + a_n \\vec{n} = \\frac{dv_\\tau}{dt}\\vec{\\tau} + \\frac{v_\\tau^2}{\\rho}\\vec{n}$, where $a_\\tau$ modulates speed and $a_n$ modulates direction",
      "Total acceleration magnitude: $w = |\\vec{a}| = \\sqrt{a_\\tau^2 + a_n^2}$",
      "Analysis of spiral trajectory with $w_\\tau = a$ and $w_n = b t^4$: expressing covered path $s(t) = \\frac{1}{2}at^2$, finding dynamic curvature radius $R(s) = \\frac{a^3}{2bs}$, and total acceleration $w(s) = \\sqrt{a^2 + \\left(\\frac{4bs^2}{a^2}\\right)^2}$"
    ]
  }
]
